name: Vegetation and fire exposure
instruction: Walk the outside of the house and photograph the gap between the walls and any vegetation.
tips: The front elevation, from the street
Each remaining side and the rear, from far enough back to show the gap between wall and vegetation
The 0–5 ft strip against the foundation — mulch, shrubs touching siding
The roof edge and gutters from the ground, including any overhanging canopy
The downslope, if the lot is graded

requiredElements.description: The base of an exterior wall where it meets the ground
The strip of ground immediately against that wall

checks.lookFor: Shrubs, branches or climbing plants touching or overhanging the siding, wall or roof edge
Bark mulch, dry grass or leaf litter laid against the foundation within roughly five feet of the wall
Tree canopy extending over the roof or within a few feet of the roof edge

name: Roof, eaves and vents
instruction: From the ground, photograph the largest visible roof slope, then follow the edge round to the eaves. Do not climb.
tips: Shingles or tiles in focus — patches, gaps or missing pieces
The eaves and any soffit or gable vents, close enough to see whether they are screened
Debris sitting in the valleys or along the roof edge

requiredElements.description: A section of roof covering — shingles, tiles or metal
The roof edge or eave line

checks.lookFor: Missing, cracked, curling or patched shingles or tiles
Soffit, gable or ridge vents with no mesh screen, or with damaged or displaced screening
checks.closeUpPrompt: We can't tell whether that vent is screened. Take one close-up of the vent opening so we can see the mesh.

checks.lookFor: Leaf litter, needles or branches accumulated in valleys or along the roof edge

name: Gutters, downspouts and drainage
instruction: Photograph one downspout from the gutter seam above it down to where the water lands.
tips: The gutter seam above, and any debris sitting in the trough
Where the water exits at the bottom
The ground below the spout — splash block, erosion, or water running back toward the house

requiredElements.description: A downspout running down the wall
The ground where the downspout discharges

checks.lookFor: Leaves, needles or silt visible in the gutter trough, or plants growing from it
Downspout discharging directly against the foundation with no splash block or extension
Soil erosion, pooling water or a washed-out channel at the discharge point
Downspout sections separated, crushed or hanging away from the wall

name: Deck, porch and stored combustibles
instruction: Photograph any attached deck or porch, including what is stored underneath it and against the house.
tips: The deck surface and where it meets the wall of the house
Underneath the deck — stored wood, furniture, or built-up leaf litter
Firewood, propane tanks or bins stacked against the walls

requiredElements.description: The deck or porch surface
Where the deck meets the wall of the house

checks.lookFor: Firewood, cardboard, furniture or bins stacked under the deck or against the house wall
Propane or fuel cylinders standing against or close to the wall of the house
Built-up leaf litter or dry debris in the space beneath the deck
Soft, darkened, split or visibly rotting deck boards or support posts

name: Water heater
instruction: Stand about six feet back and photograph the full unit, showing the tank, the floor, and the immediate surroundings.
tips: The top of the unit: supply connections, fittings, and the T&P valve with its discharge pipe
The base of the tank and the floor: drip pan, rust at the bottom seam, staining
The data plate or label — the serial number tells us the manufacture date

requiredElements.description: The whole height of the tank, top to bottom
The base of the tank and the floor beneath it
The pipe connections at the top of the unit

checks.lookFor: Rust, flaking or corrosion at the bottom seam of the tank or on its base ring
Water staining, mineral crust or damp patches on the floor around the tank
Tank standing directly on the floor with no drip pan beneath it
Temperature and pressure relief valve with no discharge pipe, or a pipe that ends well above the floor
Signs the unit is old — a dated or corroded data plate, heavy scale, or outdated fittings
checks.closeUpPrompt: The unit looks past ten years old. Add a close-up of the data plate so we can confirm its age from the serial.

name: Main water shutoff
instruction: Photograph the main shutoff valve for the whole house, with enough around it to show where it is.
tips: The valve handle, close enough to read any label
The pipe on either side of the valve
The route you would take to reach it in a hurry

requiredElements.description: The shutoff valve itself, handle included
The pipe running into and out of the valve

checks.lookFor: Rust, green corrosion or mineral crust on the valve body, handle or adjoining pipe
Stored items, shelving or clutter blocking access to the valve
Damp, drips or fresh staining at the valve stem or its joints
checks.closeUpPrompt: There may be moisture at the valve. Take one close-up of the valve body so we can tell a fresh drip from an old mark.

name: Electrical panel
instruction: Open the panel door — the outer door, not the cover — and photograph the breakers and their labels.
tips: All breakers, with the labels readable
The brand label on the panel
Any rust, scorching or discoloration

requiredElements.description: The rows of breakers inside the open panel
The interior face of the panel around the breakers

checks.lookFor: Scorch marks, browning, melted plastic or heat discoloration on breakers or the panel face
Rust or corrosion inside the panel enclosure or on the breaker faces
Breakers with blank, illegible or handwritten-over labels
More than one wire landed under a single breaker terminal

name: Furnace, air handler and condensate line
instruction: Photograph the furnace or air handler from far enough back to see the whole unit and the floor beneath it.
tips: The manufacturer label
The condensate line and its drain pan
Any staining or rust on the pan or the floor below

requiredElements.description: The whole furnace or air handler cabinet
The floor and any drain pan directly beneath the unit

checks.lookFor: Standing water, sludge or mineral crust in the condensate drain pan
Condensate line disconnected, kinked, sagging or discharging onto the floor
Rust streaks or corrosion on the cabinet, pan or the floor beneath the unit
Boxes, textiles or stored items stacked against the furnace cabinet

name: Washing machine hoses
instruction: Pull the washing machine forward if it is safe to do so and photograph the hoses at the back.
tips: Both the hot and cold hoses, end to end
The wall valves they connect to
The floor beneath — staining, or a drain pan if there is one

requiredElements.description: The supply hoses running from the wall to the machine
The wall valves the hoses connect to
The floor behind and beneath the machine

checks.lookFor: Plain rubber supply hoses rather than braided stainless steel
Bulging, cracking, kinking, or rust and crust at the hose couplings
Water staining, warping or mineral residue on the floor behind the machine
Machine standing directly on finished floor with no drain pan

name: Dryer vent and lint path
instruction: Photograph the back of the dryer where the vent duct connects, then the vent's outlet on the outside wall.
tips: The duct behind the dryer — crushed, kinked or disconnected sections
Lint built up behind or underneath the machine
The exterior vent hood, and whether its flap moves freely

requiredElements.description: The vent duct where it connects to the back of the dryer
The floor and wall space behind the dryer

checks.lookFor: Lint accumulated behind or beneath the dryer, or escaping from the duct connection
Flexible foil or plastic ducting rather than rigid or semi-rigid metal
Duct crushed, sharply kinked, or separated at a joint
Duct fully disconnected from the dryer or the wall outlet

name: Under the kitchen counter
instruction: Open the cabinet under the kitchen sink and take a wide shot of the whole space, with both sides of the P-trap in frame.
tips: Both sides of the P-trap in one frame
The supply lines and both shutoff valves
The cabinet floor and base — staining, swelling, or warped particleboard

requiredElements.description: Both sides of the P-trap, in one frame
The supply lines and both shutoff valves
The floor of the cabinet beneath the plumbing

checks.lookFor: Rust, green corrosion or mineral crust on the trap, tailpiece or supply connections
Dark staining, swelling, bubbling or delaminated particleboard on the cabinet floor
checks.closeUpPrompt: We see a dark ring on the cabinet floor near the trap. Take one close-up of that spot so we can tell an active leak from an old stain.

checks.lookFor: Visible droplets, wet surfaces or a container placed to catch water
Plastic or plain rubber supply lines rather than braided stainless steel

name: Dishwasher and its supply line
instruction: Open the dishwasher door and photograph the unit, then the supply line where it runs under the sink.
tips: The floor and cabinet edge directly in front of the dishwasher
The supply line and its shutoff valve
The seal along the bottom of the door

requiredElements.description: The open dishwasher and its door
The floor and cabinet edge directly in front of the unit

checks.lookFor: Cracked, hardened, mouldy or displaced seal along the door edge
Swelling, discoloration or lifting of the flooring or cabinet edge in front of the unit
Standing water, rust or mineral residue in the base of the tub

name: Refrigerator water line
instruction: Pull the fridge forward if it is safe to do so and photograph the water line behind it.
tips: The braided or plastic line, end to end
The shutoff valve
The floor behind the fridge — staining or buckling

requiredElements.description: The water line running to the back of the fridge
The floor behind and beneath the fridge

checks.lookFor: Plain plastic or copper tubing rather than braided stainless steel
Water line kinked, pinched behind the appliance, or crimped against the wall
Staining, buckling or discoloration of the floor behind the fridge
Rust, crust or damp at the valve or the line's connections

name: Range, cooktop and hood
instruction: Photograph the range or cooktop with the hood above it in frame.
tips: The burners or cooktop surface
The underside of the hood and its filter — grease buildup
The wall and cabinets on either side of the range

requiredElements.description: The range or cooktop surface
The hood or extractor above the range

checks.lookFor: Grease accumulated on the hood filter, the underside of the hood, or the surrounding wall
Towels, packaging, curtains or plastics resting on or beside the cooking surface
No extractor hood or vent above the cooking surface

name: Under the primary bath sink
instruction: Open the primary bathroom vanity and take a wide shot of the whole space, with both sides of the P-trap in frame.
tips: Both sides of the P-trap in one frame
The supply lines and both shutoff valves
The cabinet floor and base — staining, swelling, or warped particleboard

requiredElements.description: Both sides of the P-trap, in one frame
The supply lines and both shutoff valves
The floor of the vanity beneath the plumbing

checks.lookFor: Rust, green corrosion or mineral crust on the trap, tailpiece or supply connections
Dark staining, swelling, bubbling or delaminated particleboard on the vanity floor
checks.closeUpPrompt: There may be water damage on the vanity floor. Take one close-up of that spot so we can tell an active leak from an old stain.

checks.lookFor: Visible droplets, wet surfaces or a container placed to catch water

name: Tub and shower seal
instruction: Photograph where the tub or shower base meets the wall.
tips: The caulk line, corner to corner
Grout condition on the surrounding tile
The corners, where movement shows first

requiredElements.description: The joint where the tub or shower base meets the wall
The wall surface or tile immediately above that joint

checks.lookFor: Caulk cracked, split, shrunken, lifting or missing along the joint
Grout crumbling, missing, or darkly discoloured between tiles
Black or dark mould growth along the seal or in the corners
Tiles lifting, cracked, or a wall surface that looks soft or bowed

name: Toilet supply line and base
instruction: Photograph the toilet from the side, low enough to catch the supply line and the floor at its base.
tips: The supply line and its shutoff valve
The floor where the base meets it — staining or soft flooring
Any gap or rocking where the base sits

requiredElements.description: The supply line and its shutoff valve
The base of the toilet where it meets the floor

checks.lookFor: Staining, discoloration or lifting flooring around the base of the toilet
Rust, crust or damp at the shutoff valve or the supply connections
A visible gap, failed seal or displaced trim where the base meets the floor

name: Smoke detectors
instruction: Photograph each smoke detector with enough ceiling or wall around it to establish where it is.
tips: One photo per detector, showing the unit plus its surroundings
A wide shot of the hallway outside the sleeping rooms
One photo per level of the home, so we can check coverage

requiredElements.description: A smoke detector unit
Enough ceiling or wall around it to show where it is mounted

checks.lookFor: A mounting bracket or ceiling mark with no detector on it, or a unit hanging off its base
Yellowed, dusty or visibly dated casing suggesting an old unit
Detector mounted in a corner, behind a beam, or otherwise obstructed

name: Fireplace, wood stove or chimney
instruction: Photograph the fireplace or wood stove with the floor and wall around it, then the chimney from outside.
tips: The firebox and the hearth in front of it
Anything combustible within three feet — rugs, furniture, stored wood
The chimney from the ground, including the cap and any spark arrestor

requiredElements.description: The firebox or stove body
The hearth and floor immediately in front of it

checks.lookFor: Rugs, furniture, baskets or stored wood within roughly three feet of the firebox opening
Heavy black tarry deposits inside the firebox or flue opening
Cracked, spalled or missing masonry in the firebox, hearth or surround
An open firebox with no screen or glass door fitted

name: Attic, crawlspace or basement
instruction: Photograph whichever unfinished space your home has under the roof or under the floor — only where you can reach safely.
tips: The underside of the roof deck — dark staining around nails or vents
Insulation that is compressed, discolored or fallen
The lowest point of the floor — standing water, chalky residue on walls, or a sump pump if there is one

requiredElements.description: The underside of the roof deck, a foundation wall, or the floor of the space
Enough of the surrounding space to show what kind of area this is

checks.lookFor: Dark staining or tide marks on the roof deck, joists, foundation walls or floor
Pooled water, damp soil or wet residue at the lowest point of the space
White chalky mineral residue on masonry or foundation walls
Insulation compressed, fallen, discoloured or visibly damp
Fuzzy or speckled dark growth on timber, insulation or masonry
checks.closeUpPrompt: There may be mould growth on that surface. Take one close-up so we can tell staining from active growth.
